text.p: The Philippine peso is seen consolidating in the range of 28/29 to the dollar on Friday after its sharp gains the previous day, traders said.
"It will trade in a wide band but not as wide as yesterday," a foreign bank dealer said.
The peso soared to a high of 27.65 on Thursday before closing lower at 28.
Due to the pesos' recent gains, the central bank lowered today its overnight borrowing rate to 25 percent from 28 percent.
The central bank had raised its key rate last week to a 2-1/2 year high of 32 percent to protect the peso from speculation.
Central bank governor Gabriel Singson had promised to bring down overnight rates to normal levels as soon as the market stabilises.
